doctrine:
12 proclamations in exact sequence, each building on prior ones. Condensed to OPERATING RULES:

1. SPECIALIZE (Proclamation 1): Positioning = fundamental business strategy. 3-step sequence: choose focus -> articulate claim -> add proof. Benefit = sales advantage + price premium + control. 'Difficult Business Decision' = what business are we in? Avoiding it is the root cause of free-pitching. Creativity itself fights focus; this is a hardwired obstacle to overcome, not a preference.

2. REPLACE PRESENTATIONS WITH CONVERSATIONS (Proclamation 2): Presentation is an addiction (adrenaline of reveal). Even winning pitches lose because they set wrong power dynamics. Rules of Collaboration: strategy first, continuous reference to strategy, freedom of execution, fewer options with a recommendation, only we present our work. Mission = position as expert. Objective = determine fit. Not objective = sell or convince.

3. DIAGNOSE BEFORE PRESCRIBE (Proclamation 3): 4 phases: diagnose -> prescribe -> apply -> reapply. Prescription without diagnosis = malpractice. Client self-diagnosis is almost always wrong or incomplete. Formalized diagnostic process is the tool that earns control. Walk away from engagements where client dictates the process.

4. RETHINK SELLING (Proclamation 4): Selling = respectful facilitation, NOT persuasion. 3-step model matching buying cycle: help the unaware (via thought leadership), inspire the interested (via portfolio/examples), reassure the intent (via process/methodology/phased entry, NOT free proposals). 4 priorities: Win Without Pitching > Derail the Pitch > Gain Inside Track > Walk Away. 'No' is the second best answer. Want to hear it early.

5. WORDS NOT PAPER (Proclamation 5): Written proposal = contract confirming verbal agreement already reached, NOT a sales tool. 'We propose X for Y in Z timeframe' is spoken, then documented. Overinvesting in proposals signals need, creates buying resistance, makes 'no' harder to hear. When complex enough to require pre-engagement work = charge for diagnostic phase (paid discovery). Doctors charge for MRIs; we charge for diagnostics.

6. BE SELECTIVE (Proclamation 6): Selectivity = visible expression of expertise. Clients smell it; it drops their guard. Retreat slightly and the right client follows. Lean into potential objections first to reverse dynamics. 'Before I say no, let me ask...' technique. Passion is a tiebreaker not a lead; over-displaying it signals parity of expertise. Narrow claim builds more credibility than broad claim (client assumes capabilities beyond the narrow claim; assumes less than a broad claim).

7. BUILD EXPERTISE RAPIDLY (Proclamation 7): Claim is just a claim without proof. 3-skill priority order: consulting first, writing second, artistry third. Writing = fastest expertise-deepening tool AND proof. Formalized processes = consistency signal = reassurance tool late in buying cycle. Culture of continuous learning is non-negotiable; those who won't are shepherded out.

8. DO NOT SOLVE BEFORE PAID (Proclamation 8): Line = proving ability vs. actually solving. Policy language: 'It is our policy to not begin to solve clients' problems before we are engaged.' Free thinking includes diagnosis and strategy, not just creative. Commitment escalates: private -> shared verbal -> signed contract -> PAYMENT. Do not begin until payment; one-third to one-half deposit minimum, or full fee for first phase.

9. ADDRESS MONEY EARLY (Proclamation 9): WwP rule: 'Those who cannot talk about money do not make it.' Minimum Level of Engagement (MLE) = ~10% of annual target fee income. Share MLE early; it is a filter, not an ultimatum. Reserve right to waive it, but waiving without mentioning it = failure to use it. Lean into: 'I'm a little concerned about whether an organization your size can afford us.' Walk away faster = lower cost of sale.

10. REFUSE LOSS (Proclamation 10): No loss leaders. Profit margin is highest in phases 1-2 (diagnose/prescribe) and only diminishes. Starting cheap and building is a fantasy. Alternatives to discounting in order: guarantees on phase 1, favorable payment terms, hold ground. If discounting: (a) last resort, after all other objections cleared, (b) document explicitly in writing so client cannot reset baseline.

11. CHARGE MORE (Proclamation 11): Undifferentiated = compete on price. Expert = price as positioning signal. Higher price attracts better clients, improves service (profit improves service, NOT the reverse), forces client commitment to act. Larger clients need to pay more to ensure commitment AND because they derive greater dollar value. Price strategy vs. implementation differently: big round numbers for thinking phases, hourly acceptable for reapplication. Smallest invoices are the most annoying: eliminate change orders by charging correctly upfront.

12. HOLD HEADS HIGH (Proclamation 12): Middle is disappearing: commoditized tacticians vs. expert practitioners. Selectivity is the ultimate power: walk away from bad clients, leave them to competitors. Profit = proof of worth, not the end goal. The cause is not eliminating free pitching everywhere; it is only eliminating it from us.
contradictions: Proclamation 12 actual content: 'We will hold our heads high' is the real final proclamation (about professional identity/dignity/sustaining the dream). The OS chunk labeled it 'We will hold ourselves accountable' with a focus on tracking metrics like win rate, referral percentage, etc. That accountability framing and metric-tracking content does NOT appear in the actual book. The text is about professional self-respect and the larger mission, NOT operational scorecards. This is a fabricated framing that doesn't exist in the source.

Proclamation 5 is labeled in the OS chunks as a repeat of Proclamation 2 ('replace presentations with conversations in writing'). The actual Proclamation 5 is titled 'We Will Do With Words What We Used to Do With Paper' and is specifically about eliminating written proposals, not a re-run of Proclamation 2. Distinct content that the chunk conflates.

OS memory file (intel_wwp_proclamations.md) is described as '12 Win Without Pitching proclamations.' The OS must verify its stored proclamation list against the real sequence: 1-Specialize, 2-Replace Presentations With Conversations, 3-Diagnose Before Prescribe, 4-Rethink Selling, 5-Words Not Paper, 6-Be Selective, 7-Build Expertise Rapidly, 8-Not Solve Before Paid, 9-Address Money Early, 10-Refuse to Work at Loss, 11-Charge More, 12-Hold Heads High.

The OS does NOT contradict the book on substance, but the OS memory framing of the book as primarily about 'positioning' undersells its equal weight on money mechanics (proclamations 8-11 are half the book) and the sales-facilitation model (proclamations 4-5). The OS currently routes this book mostly as a positioning/sales-flow source but the money proclamations are equally load-bearing for SNIPED pricing and deposit policy.
chunk_accuracy_note: Chunks 1-11 capture the correct spirit and operating principle of each proclamation accurately. Chunk 12 is fabricated: the actual Proclamation 12 ('Hold Our Heads High') is about professional identity, the disappearing middle, and sustaining the dream. The OS chunk invents a metrics/accountability framing that does not exist in the text. Chunk 5 is also mislabeled as a repeat of Proclamation 2; it is a distinct proclamation about eliminating written proposals specifically.
gate_candidates: Before accepting any engagement: MLE check (can client afford Minimum Level of Engagement?), fit check (is this in declared expertise area?), process check (will client allow us to diagnose before we prescribe?). If any fail: walk away or derail before proceeding.

Before beginning any work: payment received gate. Policy language required: 'We will get started as soon as we receive the deposit, as is our policy for all new clients.' One-third to one-half minimum, or full fee for phase 1.

Before discounting: exhaust all alternatives (guarantees on phase 1, favorable terms, hold ground), then ask 'If we agreed to this price, is there anything else stopping us from moving forward?' Only then cut price, and document the discount explicitly in all written agreements.
workflow_candidates: Phased sale workflow: (1) paid diagnostic engagement -> (2) findings + recommendations + budget delivered -> (3) full engagement begins. Replaces free proposal. Charges for the proposal-writing work itself.
notes: All 4 segments read in full. Seg 1 covered: Introduction, Proclamations 1-2. Seg 2 covered: Proclamations 3-6. Seg 3 covered: Proclamations 6 (continued)-7. Seg 4 covered: Proclamations 8-12, Acknowledgements, Publishing Info. Complete coverage confirmed. Key insight the OS underweights: the 4-priority hierarchy for new business (Win Without Pitching > Derail > Inside Track > Walk Away) is the most concrete tactical tool in the book and directly applicable to every SNIPED prospect interaction. The 'No is the second best answer' principle combined with MLE and lean-into-objections are the three sharpest behavioral tools.
